headline: Malaysia’s Anthony Loke Resigns as Transport Minister Over Najib House-Arrest Pardon
seoTitle: Anthony Loke Resigns as Malaysia Transport Minister Over Najib Pardon | FMB News
seoDescription: Malaysia’s Anthony Loke announced his resignation as transport minister after Najib Razak was granted a conditional pardon allowing house arrest, while DAP said it would remain in Anwar Ibrahim’s government.
deck: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said he will leave Malaysia’s Cabinet in response to the conditional pardon allowing former prime minister Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest. DAP’s other ministers will remain in government.
author: FMB News World Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Malaysia’s Democratic Action Party secretary-general Anthony Loke announced on September 19 that he will resign as transport minister after the party’s Central Executive Committee met for nearly three hours to decide its response to the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Najib Razak.

Loke said the resignation applies only to him. Other DAP ministers and deputy ministers will remain in Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s unity government, a decision Loke said was intended to avoid political instability. He said he would submit his resignation letter to Anwar; independent reporting indicates the formal submission is expected on September 21.

sections.heading: Why Loke is resigning
paragraphs: Loke said DAP respects the King’s constitutional authority to grant pardons but finds the decision to allow Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest difficult to accept. His resignation is therefore a political response to the pardon, not a withdrawal of DAP from the governing coalition.

sections.heading: What is confirmed about Najib’s pardon
paragraphs: Malaysia’s Legal Affairs Division announced on September 18 that the Federal Territories Pardons Board granted Najib a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine and compliance with specified conditions.

The pardon does not erase Najib’s conviction and does not resolve his other pending legal proceedings. Malaysia’s Home Ministry said on September 19 that it was still awaiting formal written notification before implementing the house-arrest arrangement, so the operational transfer from prison remained unresolved at the time of publication.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: DAP is a major component of Anwar’s governing coalition. Loke’s decision creates a prospective Cabinet vacancy and publicly exposes disagreement inside the coalition over the treatment of Najib, while DAP’s decision to keep its other ministers in government limits the immediate threat to coalition stability.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The next confirmed steps are Loke’s formal submission of his resignation, Anwar’s response and any appointment or interim arrangement at the Transport Ministry. Separately, authorities still need to implement the conditions and procedures governing Najib’s house arrest.

verificationNotes: Reuters, Malay Mail and South China Morning Post independently report Loke’s September 19 announcement and carry his direct statement that he will resign as transport minister.
Reports agree that Loke’s resignation applies only to his Cabinet post and that other DAP ministers will remain in the unity government.

The underlying Najib conditional pardon was announced September 18 by the Legal Affairs Division under Malaysia’s Prime Minister’s Department; the pardon permits house arrest until August 23, 2028 subject to conditions including payment of the RM50 million fine.

Malaysia’s Home Ministry said September 19 it had not yet received the formal written notification needed for implementation; the article therefore does not state that Najib had already been transferred to house arrest.

Wikimedia Commons identifies the Anthony Loke portrait as C.W. Tan’s own work and licenses it under CC BY-SA 4.0. The caption labels it as a 2023 file photograph and does not imply it depicts the 2026 announcement.
No successor to Loke was confirmed at publication time.
